thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: multiple container restarts detected in us-east-1 pool-7. Reason: GPU OOM during prefill. Pager auto-triggered.

maria: oncall here, taking it. tagging @alex for infra assist.

alex: ack, joining. any customer-facing impact yet?

kevin: spike in restarts on node-7c3 and node-7d1, ~3-6 restarts/min. kube shows OOM kill from nvidia driver.

kevin: log snippet:```
2026-03-17T08:12:02Z runtime: CUDA out of memory while allocating 104857600 bytes
stack: serve.prefill() -> kv_cache.alloc() -> cudamalloc()
session: sess-9f2a, prompt_len: 187k tokens, model: redwood-13b-v2
container: pool-7/replica-12 restarted (exit code 137)
```

jordan: CS ping — customer acme-docs is seeing 503s and retries, reported around 08:11 UTC. I told them we are investigating.

emily: metrics: median prefill time spikes, GPU mem utilization saturates to 100% during prefill window, then OOM. Prefill queue length increased too.

maria: initial hypothesis: very large context/prompt hitting kvcache + prefill allocation path -> OOM. Could be long prompts from client streaming in entire context.

alex: mitigation plan: 1) stop scheduling new sessions to pool-7 hot nodes 2) cordon node-7c3 3) apply prefill token cap and prefix trimming policy for pool-7 4) rollout hotpool add capacity

kevin: cordoning node-7c3 now -> `kubectl cordon node-7c3`

incident-bot: ACTION: node-7c3 cordoned by kevin at 08:15 UTC

emily: issuing scaledown of problematic replicas and draining to avoid noisy restarts: `kubectl drain node-7c3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

jordan: CS note: let me know when we have a mitigation message I can send to AcmeDocs. They asked for ETA.

maria: temporary config change: set max_prefill_tokens=8192 for pool-7 and enable prefix_trim=true. Applying to canary nodes first.

alex: rolling canary change to 2 nodes in pool-7: `/ops/configs/apply --pool pool-7 --canary 2 prefill.max_tokens=8192 prefill.prefix_trim=true`

incident-bot: DEPLOY: config rollout started for pool-7 (canary 2/2) at 08:18 UTC

kevin: canary nodes look stable for 5m, no OOMs in logs. Promoting to remaining hotpool replicas.

emily: after promoting, overall restart rate dropped to ~0-1/min. GPU mem utilization now peaks lower (~78%).

maria: routing change: for sessions >64k token estimates, route to smaller model variant (redwood-7b-quant) as fallback until further tuning. Implementing via routing policy change.

alex: routing flag toggled: `route.large_context_to=fallback-7b` for pool-7.

cs_liaison: message for AcmeDocs drafted: "We've identified GPU OOMs on a subset of nodes caused by very large context prefill. We've applied temporary caps and routing fallbacks; service is recovering. We'll follow up with a timeline and permanent fix." Want to send?

jordan: send now, include ETA ~30m for full recovery.

maria: pager update: oncall will continue to monitor for 1h. Next steps: investigate why kvcache allocation doesn't fail gracefully for prefill (OOM should trigger graceful fallback), add prefill size autoshedding, and add a per-customer prompt-size policy.

alex: filing incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime for postmortem and remediation (tags: prefills, kvcache, routing).

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated (partial) — customer impact reduced. Follow-up required.

kevin: quick note — evicted and restarted 3 replicas, no further node flaps observed.

emily: monitoring alert set: alert if container restarts >3/min in pool-7 for 10m.

maria: thanks team. I'll handoff to oncall rotation in 30m with checklist. Postmortem owner: @alex.

jordan: CS update sent to ACME. They acknowledged, still watching.

maria: closing channel for active mitigation. keeping thread for follow-ups.
